proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(a=a_{\mathrm w}\).  We construct the unspecified variables on one probability space, conditional on \(E_0\), and use the same design and donor laws for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).  Take the displayed point \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d\) as the conditional donor mean.  Independently over \(t\), let \(X_{1t}\) be uniform on \([0,1]^d\).  Conditional on the complete design, draw the historical sign pairs independently over \((t,i)\), with
\[
 P_\rho(U_{1ti}=u,V_{1ti}=v\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 =\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4},
 \qquad (u,v)\in\{-1,1\}^2.
\]
The bound \(\sup_x|\rho(x)|\le 1-2\delta_0\), which is part of the definition of \(\mathcal R\), implies that each of these four probabilities is at least \(\delta_0/2>0\); their sum is one.  Independently over \(i\), draw the event sign pairs from the analogous conditional kernel at \(x=z_0\).  Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 B_{1i}(0)&=(1+aU_{1i})(1+aV_{1i}),\\
 B_{1i}(1)&=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1,\\
 Q_{1ti}(0)&=Q_{1ti}(1)=Q_{1ti}
 =(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti}).
 \end{split}
\]
Equivalently, set \(W_{1i,-1}=1\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=aU_{1i}\), \(R_{1i1}(0)=aV_{1i}\), and \(R_{1ih}(1)=0\) for \(h=0,1\).  Thus the displayed formula for \(B_{1i}(a)\) follows from \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  For every assignment vector define \(B_{1i}(a,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(a)\).  These definitions verify, respectively, \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}.  They also respect the return support because \(-a>-1\).

We next give a donor completion that uses the full stacked covariance.  Since \(S=1\), the donor dimension \(Sd\) equals \(d\).  Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), conditionally on \(E_0\), be independent and uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius \(\sqrt d\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), independent of the design, historical outcomes, and event outcomes, and set
\[
 Z_j=z_0+\xi_j.
\]
Rotational invariance and the identity \(\operatorname{tr}\mathbb E(\xi_j\xi_j^\top\mid E_0)=d\) give
\[
 \mathbb E(\xi_j\mid E_0)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(\xi_j\xi_j^\top\mid E_0)=I_d.
\]
Consequently the center and full conditional covariance in the frozen definitions are
\[
 \mathbb E(Z_j\mid E_0)=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_d.
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), this proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Moreover, using the hypothesis \(B\ge d^2\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[
   \left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\right\|_2^4
   \mathrel{\big|}E_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E(\|\xi_j\|_2^4\mid E_0)
 =d^2\le B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-replication}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} also hold.  In particular, no coordinatewise diagonalization is substituted for the stipulated full covariance.

We now verify the historical regression and its regularity conditions.  Summation of the four-point sign law gives, for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)=\rho(x).
\]
It follows equation by equation that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 m_1^{P_\rho}(x)
 &=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti})
      \mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\right]\\
 &=1+a\mathbb E(U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
    +a\mathbb E(V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
    +a^2\mathbb E(U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)\\
 &=1+a^2\rho(x).
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is precisely \texttt{ass:historical-regression}.  The displayed compatibility hypothesis
\(\{1+a^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}\subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\)
verifies \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}.  Since \(H=1\) and \(p\ge1\), one has \(d=2p\ge2\), and hence
\[
 0<(1-a)^2\le Q_{1ti}\le(1+a)^2<4\le d^2\le B.
\]
The same inequalities apply to \(B_{1i}(0)\), while \(B_{1i}(1)=1\le B\).  Therefore \texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth} and \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth} hold.

The conditional response-variance restriction follows from a direct calculation rather than from the construction by fiat.  Put \(U=U_{1ti}\), \(V=V_{1ti}\), and \(r=\rho(x)\).  Since \(\mathbb E(U+V)=0\), \(\mathbb E(UV)=r\), \((U+V)^2=2+2UV\), and \((U+V)UV=U+V\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 &=\operatorname{Var}\{a(U+V)+a^2UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
 &=a^2\mathbb E\{(U+V)^2\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}
   +a^4\operatorname{Var}(UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)\\
 &\quad+2a^3\mathbb E\{(U+V)(UV-r)\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
 &=2a^2(1+r)+a^4(1-r^2).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The cross term in the third line is zero because both \(\mathbb E\{(U+V)UV\}\) and \(r\mathbb E(U+V)\) vanish.  The response-variance compatibility condition in the proposition therefore yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(\varepsilon_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 =\operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 \ge B^{-1},
\]
where the equality uses \(\varepsilon_{1ti}=Q_{1ti}-m_1(X_{1t})\).  This verifies \texttt{ass:response-variance}.

The uniform design density equals one; the declared ranges \(c_X\in(0,1]\) and \(C_X\in[1,\infty)\) thus give \(c_X\le f_{1,E_0}(x)\le C_X\), proving \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Conditional independence of the sign pairs over \((t,i)\), together with independence of the event pairs, proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}; the identical conditional kernels over \(i\) prove \texttt{ass:within-site-replication}.  The complete calendar vectors are independent over \(t\) conditional on \(E_0\), so
\[
 \beta_{P_\rho}(k\mid E_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Set \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{1t}\) to obtain \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}.  The stipulated location of \(z_0\) proves \texttt{ass:interior-event-path}.  Taking the conditional event state to be degenerate at the displayed configuration gives
\[
 P_\rho\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\ge c_X,
\]
so \texttt{ass:positive-query-region} holds.  Finally, by the defining property of \(\mathcal R\), the induced surface \(x\mapsto1+a^2\rho(x)\), with the covariance \(\Sigma=I_d\) just computed, satisfies the two-sided covariance-standardized local-modulus inequalities for every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\).  This is \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

It remains to verify event transport and thereby finish the membership claim.  The event untreated signs use the same conditional kernel at \(z_0\), so the preceding mean calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
 =1+a^2\rho(z_0)=m_1^{P_\rho}(z_0).
\]
Averaging this identity over \(i=1,\ldots,n_1\) proves \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  We have now checked every member property listed in \texttt{def:panel-law-class}; hence
\[
 \{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
The family is indexed by the nonempty relatively open set \(\mathcal R\), as required.

We next derive the causal target, keeping it distinct from the historical regression.  Because \(S=1\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s=1\), one has \(\pi_1=1\).  Using \texttt{def:target}, the potential-outcome construction, and the event-transport equality proved above,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)
 &=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
   \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]\\
 &=1-\{1+a^2\rho(z_0)\}\\
 &=-a^2\rho(z_0).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the equality between the causal contrast and a function of the historical surface is a consequence of the potential-outcome definitions and \texttt{ass:event-transport}; it is not imposed as a definition.

We finally compare the restricted observed-law maps.  Marginalizing the sign-pair kernel gives
\[
 P_\rho(U=u\mid x,E_0)
 =\sum_{v\in\{-1,1\}}\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}
 =\frac12,
 \qquad
 P_\rho(V=v\mid x,E_0)=\frac12.
\]
Therefore each untreated return coordinate has, conditional on any proxy value \(x\), the same symmetric two-point law on \(\{-a,a\}\), and in particular conditional mean zero, for all \(\rho\).  Every treated return coordinate is identically zero.  The initial-wealth law is the common point mass at one, and
\(\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]=1\) for every \(\rho\).  By \texttt{def:mean-only-information},
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_\rho)
\]
is consequently constant over \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).

To obtain an explicit separated pair from relative openness, choose \(\rho_*\in\mathcal R\), which exists by nonemptiness.  Endow the Hölder ball with its Hölder-norm topology.  Since \(\mathcal R\) is relatively open, there is \(\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
 \bigl\{g\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L):
       \|g-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon\bigr\}
 \subset\mathcal R.
\]
Choose a constant function \(c\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) with \(c\ne\rho_*(z_0)\); such a choice exists because \(L>0\).  For \(0<\eta<1\), let
\[
 \rho_\eta=(1-\eta)\rho_*+\eta c.
\]
The Hölder ball is convex, so \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and
\[
 \|\rho_\eta-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}
 =\eta\|c-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon
\]
for all sufficiently small \(\eta>0\).  Relative openness then gives \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal R\), while
\[
 \rho_\eta(z_0)-\rho_*(z_0)
 =\eta\{c-\rho_*(z_0)\}\ne0.
\]
Set \(\rho^{(0)}=\rho_*\) and \(\rho^{(1)}=\rho_\eta\).  Constancy of the restricted information map and the causal-target formula yield
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
 =\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
\]
but
\[
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)
       -\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
Hence no functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) can equal \(\tau_n\) throughout this submodel.  This does not imply equivalence of the full historical wealth laws: indeed the joint sign law, and generally the conditional distribution of \(Q_{1ti}=(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti})\), varies with \(\rho\).  The conclusion is therefore exactly the asserted nonidentification under the restricted mean-only map.

Put
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}\in(0,1),
\qquad
q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}>0.
\]
The asserted ranges follow from \(\lambda>0\) and \(d>0\).  We first prove the scalar weighted arithmetic--geometric mean inequality needed below rather than invoke it externally.  For \(u>0\), define
\[
\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a.
\]
Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
\phi'(u)=a\bigl(1-u^{a-1}\bigr).
\]
Since \(a-1<0\), one has \(u^{a-1}>1\) for \(0<u<1\) and \(u^{a-1}<1\) for \(u>1\).  Hence \(\phi'\) is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on \((1,\infty)\), so \(u=1\) is a global minimizer and \(\phi(u)\geq0\).  Taking \(u=x/y\) and multiplying by \(y>0\) gives
\[
x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
\qquad x,y>0.
\]

The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) imply
\[
q(1-a)
=\frac{2\lambda}{d}\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}
=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
=a.
\]
For each \(s\), positivity of the integers \(T\) and \(n_s\) therefore permits the preceding scalar inequality with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\).  It yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=n_s^{-a}T^{-a}\\
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}\\
&\leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(T\geq1\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  The definition of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} consequently gives
\[
T^{-q}
\leq(\log2)^{-q}
\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
=(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
Multiplying the cohortwise inequality by \(\pi_s^2\) and summing gives, by the definitions of \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\) in \texttt{def:rate-frontier},
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
+(1-a)T^{-q}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2.
\]
The cohort weights are positive and sum to one, so
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2
\leq\left(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\right)^2
=1.
\]
It follows equation by equation that
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
&\leq
\bigl\{a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\bigr\}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)\\
&=C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(0<\log2<1\) and \(q>0\), whence \((\log2)^{-q}>1\) and
\[
C_{\lambda,d}=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq a+(1-a)=1.
\]

Let
\[
A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
D_0:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Every rate component is positive.  By \texttt{def:rate-frontier} and the bound just proved,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_0
&\leq R_{\star,\beta}\\
&=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\\
&\leq D_0\vee(C_{\lambda,d}A)\\
&\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_0,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last step uses \(C_{\lambda,d}\geq1\), \(A\leq D_0\), and \(D_0\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_0\).  Thus
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
The comparison constants are \(1\) and \(C_{\lambda,d}\), so they are independent of \(N\), \(T\), \(S\), and the positive replication counts; in particular the comparison is uniform for fixed \(S\).

Again by \texttt{def:rate-frontier}, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\).  Along any joint growth array, the donor channel is negligible relative to the non-donor active rate \(A\) precisely when
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\]
and it dominates that rate precisely when
\[
A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\]
The boundary relation \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\) is equivalent, because \(\kappa>0\), to
\[
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Indeed, raising the two positive sides of a two-sided constant comparison to the power \(-1/\kappa\) preserves a two-sided constant comparison, with the inequalities reversed.  Since the present argument is algebraic, these regions are minimax phases only in an experiment where a separate theorem proves that \(R_{\star,\beta}\) is the sharp risk.

For the iid-design comparator, or under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}\), repeat the cohortwise calculation without the logarithmic comparison.  It gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}\\
&\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
\end{aligned}
\]
because a convex combination of two real numbers is no larger than their maximum.  The comparator definition of \(R_\star\) in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} then implies both
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\leq R_\star
\]
and, using the preceding bound,
\[
R_\star
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} states
\[
X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}.
\]
Thus every historical-design functional used at the exact coordinate \(X_{st}\) is also a functional of the recorded coordinate; no measurement-error convolution must be inverted.  Moreover, direct inspection of the exhaustive list of rate components in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} shows that it contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate moving-Gram term.  This observation concerns only the stated observation structure and bookkeeping, and supplies no statistical sharpness assertion.

Finally, \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  If \(\lambda>1\), then \(\kappa=1\), and \texttt{def:rate-frontier} gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}=N^{-1}.
\]
This proves every asserted algebraic relation and the higher-smoothness saturation claim.

It suffices to construct one admissible triangular array.  Fix
\(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and \(\pi _1=1\).  Take
\[
B=16,\qquad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\qquad \delta _0=\frac14,
\qquad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1,
\]
and take the H\"older radius \(L\) large enough to contain the affine function below.  Let
\(K(u)={\bf 1}\{|u|\leq 1\}\).  Take \(K_D=2\) and use the deterministic
donor split whose fold sizes differ by at most one, as permitted by the
estimator construction.  Since \(r=0\), the polynomial basis is
\(b_0(u)=1\); choose the admissible normalized-shape threshold
\(0<c_G\leq1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, set \(z_0=1/2\), and put
\(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).

For each \(T\), let \(n_1=N=T^2\).  Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent
uniform random variables on \([0,1]\), and define
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\]
where the \(U_{ti}\)'s are independent Rademacher variables and are independent
of the complete design.  Thus
\[
0\leq Q_{ti}\leq16,\qquad
\mathbb E[Q_{ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t),\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(Q_{ti}-m(X_t)\mid X_t,E_0)=\frac14\geq B^{-1}.
\]
The density of \(X_t\) is one.  Moreover, the calendar vectors
\(((X_t,U_{ti})_i)_{t=1}^T\) are independent over \(t\), so their conditional
absolute-regularity coefficients are zero and hence obey
\(\beta_P(k\mid E_0)\leq\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for every admissible
\(\beta_0>0\), \(0<\rho_0<1\).

Independently of the historical sample, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where the \(V_j\)'s are independent Rademacher variables.  Then
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,\qquad
\mathbb E[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0]=1\leq B.
\]
Consequently donor replication, donor independence, ellipticity, and the stated
fourth-moment bound all hold.  Set \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), which verifies
exact observation of the training coordinates.

The local-modulus condition can be checked exactly.  For
\(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), both \(z_0+u\) and \(z_0-u\) belong to \([0,1]\)
whenever \(|u|\leq\delta\), and
\[
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|
=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|u|
=\delta.
\]
Thus the two-sided modulus holds with exponent one and the displayed constants.
The affine \(m\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_1(1,L)\), the query is at least
\(\delta_0\) from the boundary, and
\(P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\geq c_X\).

It remains to define the event outcomes.  Put
\[
G={\bf 1}\{X_1\leq1/4\},
\qquad B_i(0)=8,
\qquad B_i(1)=8+G,
\qquad B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1).
\]
Define \(B_i(a,\mathbf a_{-i})=B_i(a)\), and define every historical potential
outcome \(Q_{ti}(a)\) to equal the displayed \(Q_{ti}\).  These definitions
give consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, and limited
anticipation.  They also satisfy the support restrictions.  The buy-and-hold
construction is realized by taking \(W_{i,-1}=1\) and
\(R_{i0}(a)=B_i(a)-1>-1\), for then
\(W_{i,-1}\{1+R_{i0}(a)\}=B_i(a)\).

Because \(m(z_0)=8\), event transport follows from
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E[B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0).
\]
Conditional on the complete design, each event outcome is a constant and the
historical error path of unit \(i\) is a function only of
\((U_{ti})_{t=1}^T\).  Those paths are independent across \(i\).  Hence the
required conditional cross-unit independence holds, and identical conditional
laws of the \(U_{ti}\)'s give within-site replication.  This verifies every
member property in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(1)\).

By the target definition and the fact that \(G\) is Bernoulli with probability
\(1/4\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathbb E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E[G]=\frac14,
\qquad
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]
We next control the fitted untreated mean.  Under the chosen split, every
complementary fold size satisfies \(m_k\asymp N=T^2\).  Projection onto \([0,1]\) is
nonexpansive and fixes \(z_0\), so
\[
\mathbb E[(\widetilde z_{1k}-z_0)^2\mid E_0]
\leq \mathbb E\!\left[
\left\{m_k^{-1}\sum_{j\notin k}V_j\right\}^2\right]
=m_k^{-1}=O(T^{-2}).
\]
The initial log-adjusted bandwidth in the feasible estimator is, for all large
\(T\),
\[
\underline h_T
=C_h\left[(Tn_1)^{-1/3}
\vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}
\vee N^{-1/2}\right]
=C_h\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T.
\]
Conditional on any \(\widetilde z_{1k}\in[0,1]\), the intersection of
\([\widetilde z_{1k}-\underline h_T,
\widetilde z_{1k}+\underline h_T]\) with \([0,1]\) has length at least
\(\underline h_T\).  Donor independence and the uniform design therefore give
\[
P\!\left\{
\sum_{t=1}^T K\!\left(\frac{X_t-\widetilde z_{1k}}
{\underline h_T}\right)=0
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_{1k}\right\}
\leq(1-\underline h_T)^T
\leq e^{-T\underline h_T}.
\]
A union bound over the fixed number \(K_D\) of folds shows that the event
\(\mathcal A_T\), on which every initial window is nonempty, has probability
tending to one.  On a nonempty order-zero fit,
\(G_{1k}(h)/L_{1k}(h)=1\); hence the normalized-shape rule selects
\(h_{1k}=\underline h_T\) on \(\mathcal A_T\).

Let \(I_k=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z_{1k}|\leq\underline h_T\}\).  On
\(\mathcal A_T\), the fold intercept is
\[
e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{1k}
=\frac1{n_1|I_k|}\sum_{t\in I_k}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{ti}.
\]
Its conditional-mean part differs from \(m(z_0)=8\) by at most
\(\underline h_T+|\widetilde z_{1k}-z_0|\), because \(m(x)-m(z_0)=x-z_0\).
Conditional on the design and donors, its error part has mean zero and variance
\[
\frac1{4n_1|I_k|}\leq\frac1{4n_1}.
\]
All order-zero successful intercepts lie in \([0,B]\), while a failed-fold
contribution is zero.  Combining the last three displays, using the donor
second-moment bound and \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\), and then averaging
the fixed number of folds yields
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat m_1-m(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\}.
\]
Since the final brace converges to zero in conditional \(L^2\), the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
=\mathbb E[(G-1/4)^2]
=\frac{3}{16}.
\]

The four comparator terms are all exactly of order \(T^{-2}\):
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=n_1^{-1}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(Tn_1)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
Thus \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

For the event multiplier, all observed event outcomes equal \(8+G\), so
\[
E_{1i}=\frac1{n_1}
\{B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\}=0
\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
It follows identically that \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=0\) and
\(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\).  Nevertheless the centered event-average contribution is
\(\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]
=G-1/4\), whose conditional variance is \(3/16\).

Finally consider the interval in \(\texttt{def:honest-interval}\).  On every
successful order-zero fit, writing
\(I_k(h)=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z_{1k}|\leq h_{1k}\}\), its weights satisfy
\[
a_{ti k}=\frac{{\bf 1}\{t\in I_k(h)\}}
{n_1|I_k(h)|},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T a_{ti k}=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T|\bar a_{ti}|=\frac1{n_1}.
\]
Therefore, on successful fits,
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\!\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\!\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}=O(T^{-1}).
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), nonnegativity and unit sum of the local-constant weights,
together with their kernel support, give
\[
A_L
\leq C_{0,1}L\,\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right).
\]
Here \(D=1\), and
\[
M_4(m_k)=\frac{16}{m_k}
+3\left(1-\frac1{m_k}\right)\leq16.
\]
Since \(K_D\) and \(\alpha\) are fixed, this implies
\(q_k=O(1)\), \(\delta_k=O(m_k^{-1/2})=O(T^{-1})\), and hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
\max_k\delta_k\leq\delta_0
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), all Gram matrices are
positive, all weights and radii are finite, and the finite donor sample
covariance admits the declared spectral clipping.  Thus the declared bad-sample
event is absent on \(\mathcal A_T\) for all large \(T\).  We have proved
\[
P(\text{bad sample}\mid E_0)\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
H_\alpha\,\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_T}
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)=o(1).
\]
Also \(\widehat\tau-G=8-\widehat m_1\to0\) in conditional probability.  Since
\(|G-1/4|\geq1/4\) almost surely, the event
\(\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\}\cap\mathcal A_T\) is contained, for all large
\(T\), in the union of
\(\{|\widehat\tau-G|\geq1/16\}\) and
\(\{H_\alpha\geq1/8\}\).  Both probabilities tend to zero, while
\(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).  Hence
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0,
\]
which completes all parts of the proposition.

Condition throughout on \(E_0\) and on the complementary-fold center \(\widetilde z_{sk}=z\).  By \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, this additional conditioning does not change the conditional law of the historical calendar process, and hence does not change the geometric bound in \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  For \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and \(0<h\le1\), define
\[
 \ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),
 \qquad
 \Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^{\top}.
\]
The support and boundedness conditions on \(K\), the density bounds in \texttt{ass:design-density}, and the change of variables \(x=z+hu\) give a constant \(C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]
 \le C_0h^d.
\tag{1}
\]
There is also a uniform lower bound.  Indeed, choose \(\eta>0\) so that \(K\) is bounded below by a positive constant on \([-\eta,\eta]^d\).  For every \(z\) and every coordinate, at least one of the two coordinate directions from \(z\) remains in \([0,1]\) for distance \(1/2\).  Consequently, after the preceding change of variables, the integration region contains one of the \(2^d\) orthant boxes of side \(\eta\wedge(1/2)\).  On each such box a nonzero polynomial \(v^{\top}b_r(u)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere.  Since there are finitely many boxes and the unit sphere in the fixed-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\) is compact,
\[
 \min_{\|v\|_2=1}\int_{O}
       \{v^{\top}b_r(u)\}^2\,du>0
\]
uniformly over those boxes \(O\).  The lower density bound therefore yields constants \(c_0,C_0>0\), depending only on the fixed class and procedural constants, for which
\[
 c_0h^d
 \le \mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]
 \le C_0h^d,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[v^{\top}\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]
 \ge c_0h^d\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{2}
\]
This argument covers centers on the boundary of the cube and hence, a fortiori, the interior centers required by \texttt{ass:interior-event-path}.  Fix
\[
 0<c_G<\frac{c_0}{4C_0}.
\tag{3}
\]

We next establish the needed concentration bound directly from absolute regularity.  Let \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\) be fixed and put
\[
 b_T=\left\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\right\rceil,
\]
where \(C_\beta\) is sufficiently large that
\[
 T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A_0}.
\tag{4}
\]
Partition \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) into consecutive blocks of length at most \(b_T\), and separate the blocks into their odd and even subfamilies.  Successive blocks in either subfamily are separated by at least \(b_T\) calendar indices.  The definition of the conditional absolute-regularity coefficient implies, by replacing the blocks successively by independent copies and telescoping total-variation distances, that the joint law of either subfamily differs from the product of its block marginals by at most
\[
 C(T/b_T)\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)
 \le CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{5}
\]
For completeness, the telescoping step follows because replacing one conditional block law by its marginal changes the integral of every indicator by at most the corresponding total-variation distance; summing these changes over the blocks gives the first expression in (5).  Thus no independence assertion beyond \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} is being imposed.

Let \(F\) be either \(\ell_{z,h}\) or \(v^{\top}\Phi_{z,h}v\) with \(\|v\|_2=1\), and, for one parity subfamily, let \(W_g\) be the sum of \(F(X_{st})\) over block \(g\).  Boundedness of \(K\) and of \(b_r\) on the support of \(K\) gives
\[
 0\le W_g\le Cb_T,
 \qquad
 W_g^2\le Cb_TW_g.
\]
For the product law in (5), the block variables are independent, and (1)--(2) imply
\[
 \sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)
 \le \sum_g\mathbb E[W_g^2]
 \le Cb_T\sum_g\mathbb E[W_g]
 \le Cb_TTh^d.
\tag{6}
\]
If \(V_g=W_g-\mathbb EW_g\), expansion of the exponential series and the bounds \(|V_g|\le Cb_T\) and \(\mathbb E[V_g^2]=\operatorname{Var}(W_g)\) give, for \(0<\theta<(Cb_T)^{-1}\),
\[
 \mathbb E e^{\theta V_g}
 \le
 \exp\!\left\{
   \frac{\theta^2\operatorname{Var}(W_g)}
        {2(1-C\theta b_T)}
 \right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Multiplying (7) over the independent blocks, applying Chernoff's inequality, and choosing \(\theta\asymp b_T^{-1}\) for a deviation of size \(cTh^d\) yields
\[
 P\!\left(
  \left|\sum_g\{W_g-\mathbb EW_g\}\right|>cTh^d
 \right)
 \le C\exp\!\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right).
\tag{8}
\]
Applying (8) separately to the two parity subfamilies, using a union bound, and then using (5) gives the same right-hand side plus \(CT^{-A_0}\) for the original dependent calendar sample.

Apply this conclusion first to \(\ell_{z,h}\), and then to \(v^{\top}\Phi_{z,h}v\) on a fixed \(1/4\)-net \(\mathcal V\) of the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  The cardinality of \(\mathcal V\) is a fixed constant.  For every symmetric matrix \(A\), the elementary net inequality
\[
 \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le 2\max_{v\in\mathcal V}|v^{\top}Av|
\tag{9}
\]
follows by approximating a maximizing unit vector by an element of \(\mathcal V\).  Equations (2), (8), and (9) therefore show that, except on an event of probability at most
\[
 C\exp\!\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0},
\tag{10}
\]
the calendar-level mass and Gram matrix satisfy
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^T\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\le2C_0Th^d,
 \qquad
 \sum_{t=1}^T\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})\succeq\frac{c_0}{2}Th^d I_{q_r}.
\tag{11}
\]
Weights and local coordinates do not depend on the replicated-unit index \(i\).  Hence the quantities in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} obey
\[
 L_{sk}(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_{z,h}(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 G_{sk}(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^T\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st}).
\tag{12}
\]
It follows from (3), (11), and (12) that the candidate passes the normalized-shape rule outside the event in (10).  Thus
\[
 P\!\left\{
 L_{sk}(h)=0\ \text{or}\
 \lambda_{\min}\!\left(\frac{G_{sk}(h)}{L_{sk}(h)}\right)<c_G
 \;\middle|\;E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}
 \right\}
 \le C\exp\!\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{13}
\]
Notice that replication cancels from the ratio in (12); an upper local-mass condition was not used.

Write \(h_0=h_{s,\beta}\).  If \(h_0<1\), its definition gives
\[
 \frac{T(2^vh_0)^d}{b_T}
 \ge c2^{vd}
\tag{14}
\]
for every dyadic candidate \(2^vh_0\le1\), after choosing the fixed constant \(C_h\) sufficiently large.  If the selector has not stopped by that candidate, the candidate itself fails.  Substitution of (14) into (13), with \(A=A_0\), proves
\[
 P\{h_{sk}>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A}.
\tag{15}
\]
The assertion is immediate when \(h_0=1\).  At the terminal candidate \(h=1\), (13) gives
\[
 P\{\text{terminal-grid failure}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\}
 \le C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A}.
\tag{16}
\]

Fix \(a>0\).  The same proof of (13) may be run with an arbitrarily large exponent \(A_a>a/d+2\) in place of \(A_0\), merely by increasing the auxiliary blocking constant \(C_\beta\); this does not alter the estimator or its bandwidth grid.  The dyadic tail-sum inequality and (15), with this stronger remainder, yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}]
 &\le h_0^a
 +\sum_{v:\,2^vh_0<1}(2^{v+1}h_0)^a
 P\{h_{sk}>2^vh_0\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\}\\
 &\le Ch_0^a+CT^{-A_a}\log(T\vee2).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Here \(\sum_{v\ge0}2^{av}\exp(-c2^{vd})<\infty\).  The definition of \(h_0\), including its truncation at one, and \(A_a>a/d+2\) now imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}]
 \le C\left\{
 (Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{a/d}
 +N^{-a/2}
 \right\}.
\tag{18}
\]

It remains to verify the asserted control of the complete bad-sample event.  Because \(S\) and \(K_D\) are fixed, a union bound in (16) controls all cohort-fold fitting failures.  A successful Gram matrix is invertible by the normalized-shape rule, so all successful-fit weights are finite.  The sample covariance of finite donor observations is finite almost surely under \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}, and spectral clipping to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\) is then a defined measurable operation by \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Moreover, for every nonempty balanced donor complement, fixed \(D=Sd\), fixed \(K_D\), and fixed \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}>0\), the displayed formulas in \texttt{def:honest-interval} imply
\[
 M_4(m_k)\le C,
 \qquad q_k\le C,
 \qquad \delta_k\le Cm_k^{-1/2}.
\tag{19}
\]
Since \(m_k\asymp N\), (19) makes \(\max_k\delta_k\le\delta_0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).  For the finitely many smaller \(N\), including values producing an empty complement, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\) is bounded below by a positive constant, so their deterministic bad-event indicators are at most \(CR_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Finally, because \(A>2\lambda/d+2\),
\[
 \exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+T^{-A}
 \le C\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
 =CR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{20}
\]
Equations (16), (19), and (20), together with the definitions in \texttt{def:rate-frontier}, prove uniformly along all stated arrays that
\[
 P\{\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0\}\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{21}
\]
The uninflated smoothing-scale local count may satisfy
\[
 T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d=O(1),
\]
but the log-adjusted definition of \(h_{s,\beta}\) gives, whether or not its truncation at one binds,
\[
 Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2).
\tag{22}
\]
Equation (22), rather than a dense-local-site assumption, is exactly the concentration input in (14).  No exogenous dense-local-site or upper-local-mass condition has been imposed.
